relations.evidence: You can secure your replication using 1 of the following approaches: [Public Internet](#public-internet) [VPC Peering](#vpc-peering) [Private Endpoint Service](#private-endpoints)

relations.subject: capella:xdcr
relations.evidence: VPC Peering can secure XDCR by replicating data over a private network. This approach avoids exposure to the public Internet and provides stronger network isolation than public Internet connectivity.

relations.subject: capella:xdcr
relations.evidence: Private endpoints expose a service-specific endpoint for XDCR, allowing clusters to replicate without network-level peering or public Internet exposure.

relations.subject: security:vpc-peering
relations.evidence: Capella clusters on GCP do not support XDCR over a VPC Peering connection when both the source and target clusters: Are deployed on Capella through GCP. Have private endpoints enabled. Share the same major network prefix of either `10.x.x.x`, `172.x.x.x`, or `192.x.x.x`.

relations.subject: security:private-endpoints
relations.evidence: Clusters deployed on AWS: Can have a maximum of 20 nodes. If you previously contacted Capella Support to map Query nodes separately with 1:1 node mapping over private endpoints, enabling XDCR over private endpoints limits your cluster to a maximum of 13 nodes.

relations.subject: security:private-endpoints
relations.evidence: [Enabling XDCR over a private endpoint connection](#enable-pe-xdcr) is only available through the [Management REST API](../../management-api-reference/index.md#tag/Private-Endpoint-Service).

notable_absence.finding: This page - the one this batch was specifically written to check - contains ZERO mentions of a privilege, an RBAC role beyond the pre-existing capella-role:project-owner, a credential *type* (Basic/Advanced), or an edition badge. Its entire security model is a choice among three NETWORK connectivity mechanisms (Public Internet, VPC Peering, Private Endpoint Service), gated by CSP, node count, and server version - not by identity or authorization at all. This directly answers the batch's central question.

cross_component_finding: DEFINITIVE ANSWER to this batch's hypothesis: manage-xdcr-security.md does NOT reveal a genuinely new access-control mechanism for XDCR. 'Security' on this page means network-transport security (which pipe the replication traffic travels over), not authentication/authorization - and even that transport-security vocabulary is a full reuse of concepts already promoted from cloud/security/security.json (security:vpc-peering, security:private-endpoints), plus one newly-named sibling (security:public-internet) that fills out a triad the registry had left implicit. The only Capella-role gate on this page is the same capella-role:project-owner already used everywhere else for cluster/project-scoped management actions. XDCR is therefore NOT a case like Sync Gateway's channel model or the Java SDK's transaction layer - it introduces no distinct access-control primitive of its own; it fully reuses the existing capella-role/credential vocabulary and layers a purely network-topology choice on top.
